pattern.crimePattern: the landowners' own advocate, who registered their "lease advances" as land transfers, kills the conservancy manager who found out and takes the original leases
pattern.notes: Fictional conservancy, trust, company and registry clerk. Close to real land disputes in the Mara, so the cultural reader is asked to check the lease model, trusts, cash advances and the registry process in Narok. No real advocate or official is portrayed.

ob.text: Rangers report the conservancy manager, Salaton Koikai (47), found dead in the archive room of the Enkare Conservancy headquarters at 06:15. The landowners' meeting he had called for 10:00 today has been postponed.

reconstruction.text: Over six months, Mvua Holdings pays cash "lease advances" to 60 landowning families. Their trusted advocate, Doreen Kathambi, reads the papers to them as advances. They are transfer forms, on paper from a shipment like the one seized at Shimanzi.
She presents all 60 at the Narok lands registry. 8,000 acres at the heart of Enkare, the lodge site included, become Mvua's. Mvua pays her KSh 600,000 a quarter.
This quarter Salaton runs registry searches, has Lornah hold the 60 payments, and calls the landowners to a meeting for Saturday at 10:00. "Bring the originals."
Friday 19:05, Doreen calls him. At 21:00 her car passes the gate. Isaiah waits at the wheel by the ranger base.
About 21:40, in the archive, Salaton shows her the original leases. She strikes him with the brass base of the desk lamp. Her scarf catches on a shelf bracket as she clears "Families 101–160".
22:40, out through the gate. By 00:45 she is in Narok, locking two boxes of leases in her office safe, on top of Mvua's payment slips and a thin folder marked in pencil.

afterVerdict.beat: Under an acacia at HQ, the 60 families' original leases are handed back to the trust. The registry transfers are frozen pending a court case. Tipape stands up and tells everyone what he signed and why. Nobody shouts at him.

Pattern File: the transfers (t_mvua, t_stamp) and the paper batch (t_stamp) are pinned. Under the payment slips in Doreen's safe, a thin folder labelled in pencil "Leverage — E.W." A photocopied police file: surveyor J. Mwenda's complaint about pressure over Bahati Block 9. "Action: NFA. Signed: E. Wairimu, Ch. Insp." Dated three weeks before Joseph Mwenda died. The signature is the one on every training memo on Amani's desk. Mwalimu's card gets a new label, "E.W.", and her portrait appears for the first time, small, pinned beside the folder.
Amani's desk phone rings. It is Mwalimu.
